section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch14 — Guidance & Counselling
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: The key difference between guidance and counselling is that:

options.option_text: Guidance is broader and often given in groups; counselling is a deeper, one-to-one, individualised process
Guidance is always one-to-one, while counselling is always in groups
Guidance and counselling are simply two names for the identical process

explanation: Guidance is a general, often preventive service given to groups; counselling is specialised, confidential, one-to-one, addressing a specific difficulty in depth.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch14 — Guidance & Counselling
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: In Carl Rogers' client-centred counselling approach, the counsellor's primary role is to:

options.option_text: Offer unconditional positive regard and empathetic listening, helping the client find their own solutions
Tell the client exactly what decision to make
Analyse the client's unconscious childhood conflicts in depth
Administer medication for the client's problems

explanation: Rogers' humanistic, client-centred approach emphasises empathy and unconditional positive regard, empowering clients to reach their own insights.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch13 — Assessment & CCE
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A test that reports a student's score as 'mastered 8 out of 10 specified learning objectives', regardless of how other students performed, is:
explanation: Criterion-referenced tests measure performance against a fixed standard, independent of peer performance. Norm-referenced tests compare a student's score to a reference group.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch13 — Assessment & CCE
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A weighing scale that consistently shows 2 kg more than a person's actual weight, every single time, is:
explanation: Reliability means consistency (same error every time); validity means measuring accurately what it claims to. A consistently wrong instrument is reliable but not valid.
